js: src/citymap.js (THREE.MeshStandardMaterial's native vertexColors — never a dedicated JS file; three.js samples mesh vertex colour for free, URP's stock Lit does not)
note: docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap A: '4 painted styles and the loggia buckets fall back to a flat colour because URP's stock Lit does not sample vertex colour.' Assets/Shaders/CityWall.shader (243 lines) is a hand-rolled URP shader modelled on Assets/Shaders/PlaneHull.shader's pattern (GetMainLight/GetAdditionalLight/SampleSH rather than UniversalFragmentPBR, for the same API-stability reason PlaneHull gives) that multiplies albedo by the mesh's own vertex COLOR — the one thing BuildRich already bakes (real OSM building:colour on 40 buildings + the style chain's hue casts on thousands more) that nothing before this displayed. CityMaterials.Build() now picks CityWallShader() for EVERY wall:*/roof:* bucket (painted AND textured, not only the 4 named in the quality-bar entry) rather than switching shaders per-bucket, for one structural reason spelled out in both files' headers: BuildingBuilder.BuildRich's wall/roof meshes carry no TANGENT stream (grepped — BuildRich never calls SetTangents/RecalculateTangents, and BuildingBuilder.cs is off-limits to add it), so stock URP Lit's normal mapping would light flat/broken once Part B's real bump maps are bound. CityWall.shader sidesteps that trap entirely with a per-FRAGMENT cotangent frame built from ddx/ddy of world position and UV (the standard tangent-free normal-mapping trick) — correct lighting with zero dependency on a vertex stream BuildRich doesn't produce. pb: photo facades are untouched (stay on stock Lit via CityMaterials.LitShader()), since they carry no meaningful per-building tint and are explicitly another agent's exclusive system. CityWallShader() falls back to LitShader() if Shader.Find fails, so a shader problem degrades to the OLD flat-colour look rather than a pink/invisible building.
verified: Assets/Editor/Probes/MaterialProbe.cs id=shader force-reimports the shader and checks ShaderUtil.ShaderHasError (PASS/FAIL printed, with the first 8 compiler messages dumped on failure, same technique as the existing ShaderErrorProbe.cs). id=buckets/assert_vertexColourShaderWired exercises every real wall:*/roof:* submesh label BuildRich emits (falling back to a direct sweep of walls.json/roofs.json + the 4 painted styles + one loggia bucket if city.json/StreamingAssets aren't present in the run) and counts how many resolve to a Material whose .shader.name == "TbilisiFly/CityWall", asserting >0. js: tools/build_wall_materials.py / tools/build_roof_materials.py (the albedo-only bake this extends — no JS equivalent, three.js never had normal/roughness maps for these tiles either)
note: docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap B, called out as 'the single biggest remaining visual gap': only albedo was ever baked for the 24 wall + 7 roof tiles (CityMaterials.cs's own prior doc comment said so outright). tools/build_tile_normals.py (311 lines, PIL 11.3.0 + numpy 2.0.2 — both already present in this environment's python3.9) derives, per tile: a tangent-space normal map from a Gaussian-blurred luminance height proxy pushed through a 3x3 Sobel gradient (edge-replicated padding, per-family depth/blur tuning — brick/stone emboss deep, plaster/panel shallow, metal modest-but-sharp), and an '_mgs.png' metallic(R)/smoothness(A) MODULATION map (both channels centred on 1.0x, derived from a local-contrast/box-blur variance measure so a busier/grimier patch of the SAME photo reads less smooth and, for metal, less uniformly metallic) — a real per-pixel roughness map, not another flat constant. Files land next to each albedo as '<stem>_n.png'/'<stem>_mgs.png' and are resolved BY FILENAME CONVENTION in CityMaterials.BindBumpAndMgs (no manifest edit needed); CityMaterials also gained MetallicFor(family) so _Metallic is no longer left at the shader's default 0 for every textured bucket. Each new PNG gets a HAND-AUTHORED Unity .meta (textureType=1/NormalMap for the _n map, textureType=0 for the _mgs map, both sRGBTexture=0 since the data is linear-encoded, never gamma-decoded) with a fresh GUID, since no agent may run the Unity editor to let AssetDatabase assign one, and a wrong default (sRGB on, Default type) would visibly break the normal map.
verified: Ran for real: `python3 tools/build_tile_normals.py` processed exactly 31/31 tiles (24 wall + 7 roof) and wrote 124 new files (31 normal PNG + 31 mgs PNG + 62 .meta). Spot-check on brick_red_n.png: R/G channel means ~127/128 (centred, i.e. real per-pixel tilt, not a flat 128 constant) with B channel mean 233.6 (mostly-upward-facing normals, consistent with a moderate emboss depth); brick_red_mgs.png R/A means ~200/213 (texture-driven variation around the 190≈1.0x baseline, not a flat uniform fill). Assets/Editor/Probes/MaterialProbe.cs id=tiles/assert_tileMapsComplete counts *.jpg vs *_n.png vs *_mgs.png in both folders via Directory.GetFiles and asserts all three equal 31 (PASS iff the Python step above has been run and its output committed) — not executed by this agent, no Unity editor access in this agent's scope; CountWithBumpMap() (CityMaterials.cs) additionally proves the maps are actually BOUND onto a real Material, not merely present on disk.

note: docs/QUALITY_BAR.md gap D. The project already decided Unity's own Scene-view Move/Rotate/Scale tools replace devmode.js's TransformControls gizmo outright ('the editor IS the gizmo') — correct for the gizmo itself, but devmode.js ALSO persists per-object position overrides to localStorage, re-applies them on load, and prints a copyable snippet, which is real functionality with no Unity-editor equivalent until this file. DevPlacement.cs (359 lines, Assets/Editor/ — uses UnityEditor APIs throughout) ports: the opt-in registry with the 'baked-collider props must not register' rule (devmode.js's own example: the tables/ranges, whose colliders are baked into a world-space soup keyed by where the code placed the mesh); EditorPrefs persistence as ONE JSON blob under one key (Newtonsoft JsonConvert, the same library CityMaterials.cs already depends on) — the direct structural analogue of devmode.js's single `tf-dev-overrides` localStorage key, including the same per-machine/non-portable trade-off the JS already had; re-application from THREE separate hooks (EditorSceneManager.sceneOpened, AssemblyReloadEvents.afterAssemblyReload, and an EditorApplication.update poll for anything registering afterward) specifically because devmode.js's own header flags a 'reload-lands-on-menu' class of bug — an object silently not reapplying its saved spot after a reload reads as a vanished edit, so this errs toward redundant re-apply paths rather than one; the copyable snippet (devmode.js:242-255) including WORLD position/yaw and lat/lon via GeoFrame.ToLatLon (Assets/Scripts/Data/GeoFrame.cs — read, not edited); and the pointer-guard (devmode.js's CLICK_PX: a press that travels less than 4px is a click, not a drag) reproduced as an epsilon guard (POS_EPS/ROT_EPS/SCALE_EPS) on the auto-commit poll, since Unity's built-in gizmo has no generic 'drag ended' event for an arbitrary registered object the way three.js's TransformControls fires 'dragging-changed' — diffing against the last-committed TRS each editor tick reproduces the same end state ('every drag is saved') without one. DevPlacementTag.cs (47 lines) is the MonoBehaviour a prop attaches to opt in — deliberately placed OUTSIDE Assets/Editor/ (a component meant to live on a scene GameObject cannot sit in a folder Unity treats as editor-only; its calls into DevPlacement are #if UNITY_EDITOR-guarded, compiling to an inert tag in a player build). NOT PORTED, by the project's own prior decision: the translate/rotate/scale mode buttons, snap toggle, world/local toggle, the in-game panel UI, the ` hotkey and click-to-select raycast — all replaced wholesale by Unity's native Scene view, which already has every one of those as a first-class feature.
